subject: SolsticeHealth hosted API - data residency and lifecycle responses
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@solsticehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Solstice hosted API - residency & retention Qs

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking our security questionnaire. We have a short set of follow-ups specific to the hosted API:

1) Where is customer data stored geographically for the hosted API (primary storage and backups)? Are there options to restrict data to a specific country/region?
2) What are your standard retention windows for request logs, prompts, model outputs, and embeddings for hosted customers? Can customers request shorter retention?
3) How do you perform deletions upon customer request? What is the expected timeline and evidence you can provide?
4) Do you maintain any long-term backups that might contain customer data beyond the primary retention period? If so, how are those handled for deletion requests?
5) Please point to any artifacts (attestations, diagrams) we can include in our SOC/Procurement review.

We are working toward a January 20 vendor cutover and need responses by Jan 14 ideally. Appreciate concise, actionable answers and any attachments.

Best,
Maya Singh
Security and Privacy Lead
SolsticeHealth

[External Sender]
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Solstice hosted API - residency & retention Qs

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers; I’ll attach a fuller bundle (diagram + exportable answers) once we finalize internal clarifications.

1) Geography: Hosted API customers are served from regional clusters. For US customers data is stored in our primary US regions (us-east-1 and us-west-2). Backups are kept in the same region by default. We offer region preference (US | EU) at onboarding for most plans; full per-country lock requires Dedicated/Private.

2) Retention windows: Request logs and tracer metadata: 90 days by default; prompts and generated outputs (application payloads): 30 days by default for hosted customers; embeddings: 90 days unless otherwise configured. Customers can request shorter retention via the console or support ticket — we have a standard 30-day retention option that is commonly applied.

3) Deletion workflow: Customer submits data erasure via Console (Data > Erase) or via support ticket. Deletion triggers a distributed wipe: (a) delete from primary DBs and object stores, (b) evict from caches and KV stores, (c) purge from index and feature stores. Expected completion: 30 calendar days from request for hosted accounts. We provide a deletion confirmation email and attestation PDF on completion.

4) Backups: We keep short-term snapshots for disaster recovery (up to 14 days) in-region; no long-term offsite backups containing customer plain-text prompts for hosted accounts. Any encrypted snapshots beyond primary retention are covered by key rotation and automated lifecycle; we can provide a backup purge attestation on request.

5) Artifacts: I will follow up with a diagram and a one-page attestation.

Let me know if you want any of these items tightened for contractual language — happy to escalate to engineering/security for a formal attestation.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Engineering (hosted API)
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Final: Hosted API data residency, retention & deletion - SolsticeHealth attestation

Maya — attaching our finalized answers and a high-level lifecycle diagram for your SOC/Procurement packet. Thanks for the deadline heads-up; we incorporated a couple clarifications from our sales/security review so this should be good for vendor intake. Below is the final summary (concise):

- Geography: Hosted API data is resident in the customer-selected region (US or EU) at account setup. For SolsticeHealth, default US cluster storage is in us-east-1/us-west-2; backups are in-region. Per-country locking is not available on hosted tier; Dedicated/Private options provide country-level guarantees.

- Retention: Audit logs (API access metadata): 365 days. Request logs/tracing metadata: 90 days. Prompts and generated outputs: 30 days (default); embeddings: 90 days. Customers may request shorter retention via Console or Support.

- Deletion: Erasure request via Console or Support triggers an automated workflow: wipe primary stores, evict caches (immediate), and purge downstream indexes/feature stores. Completion target: within 30 calendar days. Upon completion we provide a signed attestation (PDF) and an export of deletion events.

- Backups & snapshots: Short-term in-region recovery snapshots retained up to 14 days. No long-term plaintext backups retained for hosted customers. Encrypted snapshots beyond primary retention are rotated and can be destroyed; we will issue a backup purge attestation if requested.

- Evidence: Attached: 1) redwood_hostedapi_residency_answers_v1.pdf (formal Q&A + attestation) 2) data-lifecycle-diagram.png (visual flow showing storage, backup windows, and deletion steps). Also referenced: https://drive.redwood/reports/solstice-residency-answers-v1 and HubSpot ID HS-34892.

If you need this language tightened into contract-ready clauses (SLAs, indemnities), flag which items must be guaranteed and we’ll coordinate with Legal and Security to draft the wording.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Engineering (hosted API)
Redwood Inference
